report.summary: Overall the three changes work. The Dockerfile chmod lets the non-root tempo user read /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts. The R2 put mock now fails only the conversation artifact key, so other writes in the same test pass through, which removes the mockRejectedValueOnce race. The step runner test now waits on a gate instead of sleep(300). It no longer asserts that commitAndPush's recorded duration is at least 250ms, but other tests in ops.test.ts (settings.read, setup.run) still check real step durations, so that coverage remains. One problem blocks the merge: the gate uses Promise.withResolvers, an ES2024 API, but apps/tempo/tsconfig.json sets lib to ES2023. Neither worker-runtime.d.ts nor the other included types add it, so `bun run typecheck` (tsc 7.0.2) should fail with TS2550. I could not run typecheck because node_modules is not installed in this worktree.

findings.text: Promise.withResolvers is from lib.es2024.promise, but apps/tempo/tsconfig.json (and tsconfig.base.json) set lib to ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]. worker-runtime.d.ts declares no PromiseConstructor augmentation, and nothing else in the repo uses this API. The tsconfig includes `test`, so `tsc -p tsconfig.json` should report TS2550, which breaks CLAUDE.md rule 15 (typecheck must pass). Build the gate by hand instead, e.g. `let release!: () => void; const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));`. Do not raise lib, because that changes shared config.

The regression check in packages/tempod/test/image.test.ts (accessSync R_OK as tempo) only partly guards this fix. container/Dockerfile.test runs `install -d -o tempo -g tempo /opt/tempo` before the tests, so /opt/tempo is already owned by tempo and 0755. If the chmod of /opt/tempo itself were removed, the check would still pass. Only the /opt/tempo/pi part of the fix is covered. Consider checking the mode of /opt/tempo before Dockerfile.test changes it, or have Dockerfile.test copy the repo somewhere other than /opt/tempo.

Minor: the spy that wraps env.DATA.put is still named `get`. Renaming it to something like `putSpy` would make the test easier to read, and the original bound function would no longer need a separate name.
